prompt: {rider.first} carries the phone to the drinks cooler and holds the lens on {manager.first}’s face. {rider.He} {rider~wants|want} one sentence from {manager.him}, said to the strangers watching and not to the police.

exchange.line: Say it to them, {manager.first}. Not to me. To them.
Six years on this shift, {rider.first}. I don’t talk to cameras.
Then start. They’re all watching.

promptIf.prompt: {rider.first} has named the price, and {manager.first} is the one who has to pay it. {rider.He} {rider~crouches|crouch} at the cooler with the phone, waiting for one sentence.

exchange.line: You heard what I told them. One sentence.
I heard you, {rider.first}. I’m working out what I can say.
It’s one sentence. It’s one.

promptIf.prompt: {rider.first} walks the phone up close to {manager.first}. The lens is level with {manager.his} face. At the corner you watch {manager.him} look toward the stockroom door every time the phone comes up.

choices.title: Let {manager.first} answer on camera
choices.summary: {lead} offers {rider.first} what {rider.he} came for, in {manager.first}’s own voice and on camera. You don’t know what the answer is, and the handgun stays in {rider.his} hand.
choices.pull: The sentence {rider.first} came for, from the one person who can say it.
choices.cost: Every word {manager.first} says goes out live, and none of it can be taken back.

preview.favorable: {manager.first} stands at the cooler and answers into the lens, and {rider.first} hears it with every viewer.
preview.mixed: A few words come out of {manager.first} before {rider.first} cuts in and aims the lens at the chat.
preview.adverse: {manager.first} tells the stream why the account closed, a viewer types thief, and {rider.first} may level the handgun at {manager.him}.

favorable.text: {manager.first} stands with a hand on the cooler and says the sentence to the lens, not to {rider.first}. {manager.He} {manager~glances|glance} twice at the stockroom door while the viewers read it.

exchange.line: You didn’t take that bag, {rider.first}. I wrote the report and I knew it.
{manager.He} said it. Did you see? {manager.He} said it.

favorable.text: {manager.first} gets to {manager.his} feet and tells the lens what the register camera recorded. The comments freeze, then the word thief runs down the screen faster than {rider.first} can read.

exchange.line: It’s on the register camera, {rider.first}. I watched it twice.
I didn’t take it. I didn’t take it.

mixed.text: {manager.first} says {rider.first}’s name and half a sentence about the night shift. Then {rider.first} talks over {manager.him}, swings the lens to the chat and asks who believes {rider.him}.

exchange.line: Who believes me? Type it. Who believes me?

adverse.text: {manager.first} stands and tells the phone that {rider.first} lost the account over a bag that never reached its customer. A viewer types the word thief, and the replies pile up under it.

exchange.line: The order never got delivered, {rider.first}. That’s why the app closed you.

adverse.text: {rider.first} stands the phone upright on the register so it sees both of them. Then {rider.he} {rider~lifts|lift} the handgun to the height of {manager.first}’s face.

exchange.line: Now say the rest. Say it to the lens.

adverse.text: {rider.first} stops mid-word. The phone sinks to {rider.his} hip, lens down at the floor. {rider.He} {rider~answers|answer} nobody in the room or on the line.

choices.title: Turn the camera to the wall

favors.label: doesn’t speed up for the camera

choices.summary: {lead} requests that {rider.first} point the phone at the plaster and leave the sound on. The viewers get a wall, and {rider.first} gets only the negotiator’s word that it helps.
choices.pull: A quieter room, and a question {manager.first} can answer with no lens on {manager.him}.
choices.cost: The chat watches a wall and decides {rider.first} is hiding something.

preview.favorable: The camera faces the plaster with the sound on, and {rider.first} hands {manager.first} the receiver.
preview.mixed: The camera turns to the plaster, a viewer types that {rider.first} has something to hide, and {rider.first} wheels it round.
preview.adverse: A viewer reaches the front glass and films in, and {rider.first} swings the camera onto the street to show the chat.

favorable.text: The phone now faces the plaster, sound on. The comments scroll past and nobody reads them out. {rider.first} passes the receiver to {manager.first} on its cord.

{manager.first} takes the receiver and drops {manager.his} voice. {manager.He} {manager~tells|tell} the negotiator that {rider.first} never touched the bag. {manager.His} gaze stays on the stockroom door.

exchange.line: Okay. Okay. Now tell them too.

favorable.text: {manager.first} cups the receiver in both hands and speaks low. {manager.He} {manager~says|say} the register camera shows {rider.first} lifting the bag. {rider.first} hears every word.

exchange.line: Don’t tell them that. Nobody tells them that.

favorable.text: {lead} keeps the same slow pace while the comments run through the speaker.

mixed.text: The wall lasts until a comment says nobody hides a camera without a reason. Then {rider.first} swings it back to the counter and answers the commenter, not the negotiator.

exchange.line: I’m not hiding anything. I’m not hiding anything.

adverse.text: A viewer on foot slips past the tape and films the lit front glass. Then {rider.first} points the lens toward the window, so the chat can see {rider.his} audience.

exchange.line: Somebody came. Somebody actually came for me.

choices.title: Have command take the stream down
choices.summary: Your squad holds position while command calls {stream_app} and has the stream ended. The picture goes black on {rider.first}’s phone, mid-sentence.
choices.pull: The audience goes, and the negotiator is the only voice left on the line.
choices.cost: The police can switch off what {rider.first} built, and {rider.he} {rider~knows|know} who did it.

preview.favorable: The screen in {rider.first}’s hand goes dark, and {rider.first} crosses to the register phone to ask for it back.
preview.mixed: A second stream goes up on {manager.first}’s phone before command is done with the first.
preview.adverse: With the stream dead, {rider.first} sits against the cooler and tells you the bag no longer matters.

favorable.text: The picture freezes, then goes black, and the count under it drops to nothing. The register phone rings, and {rider.he} {rider~answers|answer} on the first ring.

exchange.line: Turn them back on. Then I’ll answer you.

mixed.text: The stream drops. {rider.first} takes {manager.first}’s phone off the tile and starts a second one. The old viewers find it within minutes.

exchange.line: You cut one. Go ahead, cut this one.

adverse.text: The stream ends and the phone slides out of {rider.first}’s hand onto the tile. {rider.He} {rider~sits|sit} down against the cooler, a body’s length from {manager.first}, and stops asking questions.

exchange.line: It doesn’t matter now whose hands the bag was in. Nobody’s watching.

choices.title: Move your squad up to the glass
choices.summary: {lead} walks two officers along the storefront to the front glass, a few steps from {manager.first}. The phone is aimed across the store, and the glass sits at the edge of its picture.
choices.pull: Close enough to reach {manager.first}, and to see who looks where.
choices.cost: Officers show on the stream, and {rider.first} learns where they stand.

preview.favorable: {lead} reaches the glass unseen and can watch {manager.first} while {rider.first} talks into the lens.
preview.mixed: Your officers get to the glass, but a helmet shows in the picture, and {rider.first} moves to {manager.first}.
preview.adverse: Helmets show on the screen, {rider.first} kills the front lights, and your officers lose sight of the counter.

favorable.text: {lead} settles at the glass beside a second officer, below the window line. The handgun hangs low in {rider.first}’s right hand. {manager.first} keeps glancing to the stockroom door whenever {rider.first} faces the phone.
{lead} counts the steps from the cooler to the door and finds nothing in the way.

mixed.text: The chat spots a helmet at the corner of the frame before the officers are set. {rider.first} steps over to {manager.first} and asks the line how many are outside.

exchange.line: Who is at my window? Who?

adverse.text: {rider.first} sees two helmets in the phone’s picture and flicks off the front lights. The glass goes dark for the street and for {lead}, who came to watch the counter.

exchange.line: Lights off. Let them look at nothing.
